elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty covers services only as conforming "to the requirements of this Agreement" for thirty (30) days; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Section 9 or elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "the Site and any software HDI delivers or makes available to the Company hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Period is "ninety (90) days following the Company's acceptance", not 12 months.
Services warranty runs only "for thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming Site, software or services".
"or refund the amounts paid by the Company for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty is inserted; Section 9(a) contains only corporate existence, authority, enforceability and no-conflict representations.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code, virus or disabling-device warranty appears in the inserted paragraph or elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Express software-to-documentation warranty: "for ninety (90) days following the Company's acceptance, the Site and any software HDI delivers or makes available to the Company hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — 90 days satisfies the threshold, and acceptance is an existing mechanic under Section 5.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the services performed by HDI under this Agreement will conform to the requirements of this Agreement" — a distinct 30-day services warranty separate from the software limb.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming Site, software or services".
"or refund the amounts paid by the Company for them" — refund is an available remedy for the same breach.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: Section 9 as drafted contains only mutual corporate-authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement, with no performance, conformance or remedy warranty from HDI (the Vendor), which fails the fallback on every material term.

All four fallback elements are met in operative language by the single inserted paragraph: 90-day software/Site documentation conformance, 30-day services conformance, and repair/replacement or refund as remedies. The fallback level is position-complete.

Preferred level is not complete — the workmanlike-performance standard, 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties are all absent. That is an accepted trade-off given the targeted fallback, but the drafter should not represent this as preferred.

Minimality holds: nothing existing is deleted, Sections 9(a) and 9(b) survive intact, and only one concise paragraph is added with no survival tail, procedure, notice mechanic or extra damages categories. Placing the remedy election with the Company rather than at Vendor's option is a customer-favourable variation within the remedy element, not an out-of-checklist addition.

Intent is preserved: the insertion introduces no undefined term (acceptance is an existing Section 5 mechanic; "documentation" is used descriptively), creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained Globix carve-out or the acceptance and operational-date mechanics.
Housekeeping only (not a defect in substance): the new text is appended as an unlettered paragraph after 9(b) — designate it "(c)" so the Section 9 lettering stays coherent.
